J42_migration_sources.instructions: Where should koompi-migrate look for point-fix migrations?

criteria.read_every_source: Every source the machine has, a name run once. Strongest case: a packaged machine that falls back to a checkout has a stale package directory and a current checkout, and which one is newer flips once the repo is published; per-name markers mean nothing runs twice; already built and tested. Cost: about ten more lines than one directory, and if two sources ever carried different content under one name the first source's copy wins without a word.
criteria.first_source_wins: The first source that exists, in a fixed order. Strongest case: one place to look and one rule to explain. Cost: on a packaged machine with a checkout, the source that comes first hides the other's new migrations (package first: the checkout's new fixes never run today; checkout first: the package's never run after publication).

J42_packaged_code_sync.instructions: A packaged koompi update does not run the code-tree sync (koompi-migrate --apply), so a packaged home keeps its account-creation shell and hypr/hyprland while the system copy moves. What now?

criteria.run_apply_in_packaged_update: koompi update's packaged route runs koompi-migrate --apply after pacman and before the point-fix migrations. Strongest case: without it packaged users run an old shell after every update once the repo is published, the same silent non-delivery class as the bug this round fixed; the docs promised it; --apply backs up first and spares overrides, machine-local files and set config values. Cost: an automatic rewrite of the shell tree on every packaged update, verifiable only in scratch homes until a real packaged machine exists.
criteria.leave_manual_documented: Keep it manual; the docs now say a packaged update needs koompi-migrate --apply. Strongest case: no new automatic writes into homes, and today no machine reaches the packaged route anyway. Cost: after publication, packaged users silently keep an old shell unless they know the command.
criteria.file_for_repo_publication: Record it in the open-work list (~/.config/koompi/TODO.md) as a blocker for publishing the [koompi] repo, with the failing case named, and wire it then. Strongest case: built and verified when the path can actually run, no code for an unreachable path now. Cost: depends on the note being acted on at publication.

J42_migration_failure.instructions: What should koompi update do when a point-fix migration fails?

criteria.reload_then_fail: As built: later migrations wait, the shell reloads and the hook fires, then the update exits 1 naming the failure, and the login notice offers the pending ones again. Strongest case: a migration is never load-bearing, so the new shell runs on unrepaired state, while skipping the reload leaves an old shell on new files; the user still sees the failure and a retry path.
criteria.stop_before_reload: Exit 1 before the reload and the hook. Strongest case: nothing restarts on half-applied state. Cost: new files on disk with the old shell running until next login, and the post-update hook never fires for this update.
criteria.warn_and_succeed: Warn, reload, exit 0. Strongest case: a non-load-bearing fix should not fail an otherwise good update. Cost: scripts and the updater read exit 0 as fully up to date while a fix stays pending.
